label: End of the empire
text: The Xinhai Revolution ends the Qing dynasty; the Republic of China is founded in 1912.

label: War against Japan
text: Fighting reaches Changde, the prefecture that includes Taoyuan, in 1943. Many families flee west into the mountains.

label: Battle of West Hunan
text: Japan's last major offensive in Hunan is fought in the west of the province from April to June 1945.

label: Liberation of Changde and Taoyuan
text: The People's Republic is founded in October 1949. The counties around Changde, Taoyuan among them, come under the new government between mid-July and early August 1949.

label: Rent and interest reduction
text: Before land redistribution, rents and loan interest owed to landlords are cut.

label: Land reform
text: Hunan's land reform runs from the winter of 1950 to the spring of 1952. Land is redistributed and every rural household receives a class label.

label: First Five-Year Plan
text: State-led heavy industry. Wuhan becomes a major base for steel and construction; the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens in 1957.

label: Building Wuhan Iron and Steel
text: From October 1955 about 100,000 builders from across China arrive in Wuhan to build its steel works, backed by 18 provinces, 45 cities and more than 1,000 factories. The first blast furnace produces iron in September 1958.

label: Household registration rules
text: The 1958 hukou regulations fix each person as rural or urban and sharply limit moves from countryside to city.

label: People's communes
text: Rural land and labour are organized into collectives until the early 1980s.

label: Workers sent back to the land
text: From 1961 to mid-1963 the state cuts 18.87 million workers and reduces the urban population by 26 million, mostly people recruited from the countryside since 1958.

label: Cultural Revolution
text: Families with a landlord label remain under political pressure.

label: University entrance exam returns
text: The national gaokao is restored after eleven years.

label: Reform and opening
text: Market reforms begin; the economy starts decades of fast growth.

label: Rural reform and restitution
text: Collectives give way to household farming, and restitution policies return some confiscated property.

label: Housing reform
text: Work-unit housing ends; city homes become purchases, usually with a mortgage.

label: University expansion
text: University enrolment expands rapidly.

label: WTO accession
text: China joins the World Trade Organization.

label: Urban majority
text: For the first time, more than half of China's population lives in cities.

label: Great-grandfather Li born
text: Born in the countryside of Taoyuan County.

label: Estate grows
text: With higher education and his parents' savings, he expands the family farmland; the household becomes a known landlord family.

label: Grandfather Li born
text: The eldest son is born in the home village, in the middle of the war.

label: Private school
text: At five, the eldest son starts at a private school in the home village.

label: Six months as refugees
text: The family flees to Cili County for about half a year, leaving its property behind.

label: Home again
text: Back in Taoyuan, the family runs its property again and the eldest son returns to private school, then primary school.

label: Confiscation and imprisonment
text: Land reform reaches the family. The property is confiscated, the household is left bankrupt, and Great-grandfather Li is imprisoned. His son finishes primary school and leaves for middle school in Changde.

label: College, and release
text: The eldest son, sixteen, enters an engineering college in Wuhan. The same year his father is released from prison and returned to Taoyuan for three years of labour reform.

label: Eldest daughter to Changsha
text: The eldest daughter leaves to study in Changsha. The four younger siblings stay and farm.

label: Forty-one years in steel
text: Grandfather Li joins a steel plant in Ezhou as a technician and rises to senior engineer in building design, construction, and management, retiring in 2000.

label: Eighteen years of silence
text: Because of his father's history, Grandfather Li cuts off contact with his family in Taoyuan. They do not speak again until 1981.

label: Third generation born
text: The eldest son's children are born in Ezhou.

label: Status restored, contact resumed
text: Great-grandfather Li's status is restored and he retires. His son reconnects with the family after eighteen years.

label: Property partly returned
text: Part of the property is returned and the family moves into the local town.

label: Ezhou to Wuhan
text: The third generation moves to the provincial capital and settles there.

label: Urban middle class
text: The third generation's careers grow with the economy in Wuhan.

label: Study abroad
text: With family support, the fourth generation studies in Canada: Montreal in 2022, Stanstead in 2023, Waterloo in 2026.
